verifications.claim: NASA successfully launched the Artemis II mission on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA’s Artemis II SLS ... lifted off from Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R2: 'Artemis II Launch Update: April 1, 2026'; R3: 'Artemis 2 launched on April 1'; R5: 'launched on 1 April'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm successful launch on April 1, 2026 with live updates and post-launch coverage.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch occurred at 6:24 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lifted off ... at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R2: '5:24 pm CT' (6:24 EDT window); R5: '18:35 CDT' (6:35 EDT)
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify window opens at 6:24 p.m. EDT but actual liftoff at 6:35 p.m. EDT.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch occurred at 22:24 GMT.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.reasoning: Actual liftoff corresponds to 22:35 GMT, not 22:24 GMT (window start).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch was from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida'; R2: 'NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R5: 'Kennedy Space Center'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission sends four astronauts on a 10-day crewed flyby around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon'; R3: '10-day journey'; R4: 'crewed flyby mission'; R6: '10 days'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission marks the first human lunar mission in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first crewed deep-space flight in over 50 years'; R2: 'first crewed mission ... since Apollo 17'; R4: 'first crewed flyby ... in more than 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as first in over 50 years.

verifications.claim: The crew of the Artemis II mission is Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch ... Jeremy Hansen'; identical in all sources
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew listed in every reference.

verifications.claim: The mission duration of Artemis II is ~10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'approximately 10-day'; R3: '10 days'; R6: 'MISSION DURATION | 10 days'

verifications.claim: The launch site of Artemis II is Kennedy Space Center, Florida (LC-39B).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39B in Florida'; R2: 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission was originally targeted for 2024.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Sources discuss 2026 delays but no mention of 2024 target.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II schedule was shifted to February 2026.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Sunday, Feb. 1, 2026 ... As of February 13, 2026 ... NET March 2026'
verifications.reasoning: Sources indicate February planning but shifts to March/April; not explicitly 'shifted to February' as original.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II schedule was finalized for April.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: Launch day updates April 1; R2: 'NASA has confirmed April 1, 2026'; R4: 'as soon as 1 April'

verifications.claim: Artemis II delays were due to technical issues including a helium leak.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'problem with the flow of helium to the SLS rocket’s upper stage'; also 'liquid hydrogen leaks'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly mentions helium flow issue causing delay.

verifications.claim: Artemis II delays were due to a battery issue in the Launch Abort System.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: Launch day battery sensor issue resolved without delay; prior delays attributed to helium, hydrogen leaks, not LAS battery.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Engineers have now resolved an issue ... A confidence test was performed'; R2: 'mechanical issues have been fixed/resolved'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm resolution of issues like FTS, helium, etc., before launch.
